editorial:
Imagine losing your favorite pet and then getting a replacement that can literally shoot lasers and fly. That is exactly what happens to Tyler when his inventor dad decides to build a robotic pup to cheer him up. You will quickly find that having a mechanical dog is not as simple as it sounds. The movie has a light, bouncy energy that feels like a Saturday morning cartoon come to life, blending a sweet story about grief with plenty of goofy gadget-based humor. It is a heartwarming ride that keeps things simple and fun for the whole family.

What really works here is the chemistry between the boy and his metal best friend, though the CGI can look a bit cheap in a few spots. The pacing is quick, so you will never feel bored, and the action scenes are just chaotic enough to keep you smiling. If you have kids or just want something easy to watch, you should definitely check it out. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you love collecting family gems.
endingExplained: In the final act, a greedy corporate villain tries to steal the robot dog to sell it as a weapon. Tyler and his dad have to team up to save their pet using a series of funny traps. The robot dog eventually saves the day by using a hidden super-power to stop the bad guys. In the end, Tyler realizes that while the robot is not his old dog, he can still love him as a new kind of friend.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves talking animals and gadget-filled adventures.
